feature: A press on a small or keyed layer lands on what it aims at
summary: On a small picked layer, a press on the layer itself now moves it; the depth arrow only takes a press on its own drawing. With the playhead on a key, that key's ring is drawn over the pivot crosshair and a click anywhere on it picks the key.
setup: Photonz Dev, release Next, no flag changed from its default. Walk: Scripts/playtest/small-or-keyed-layer-presses-walk.json.

try.do: Open a recording, type a title, key its Position at one second and again at three, and leave the playhead on the second key.
try.shotNote: Photographed with the window behind another app, the way a walk leaves it. Blue buttons and picked controls show their background look here; with the window in front they take the accent colour.

try.do: Click the small ring on the title's middle, a little up and right of its centre.
try.shotNote: Photographed with the window behind another app, the way a walk leaves it. Blue buttons and picked controls show their background look here; with the window in front they take the accent colour.

try.do: Drag the green flat arc sideways, then drag the blue depth arrow up and right.
try.shotNote: Photographed with the window behind another app, the way a walk leaves it. Blue buttons and picked controls show their background look here; with the window in front they take the accent colour.

try.do: Draw a rectangle about 40 points across and pick it with V.
try.shotNote: Photographed with the window behind another app, the way a walk leaves it. Blue buttons and picked controls show their background look here; with the window in front they take the accent colour.

try.do: Drag it from its upper right quarter, just beside the blue arrow: it moves.
try.shotNote: Photographed with the window behind another app, the way a walk leaves it. Blue buttons and picked controls show their background look here; with the window in front they take the accent colour.

try.do: Drag the blue arrow itself up and right: it pushes the rectangle away.
try.shotNote: Photographed with the window behind another app, the way a walk leaves it. Blue buttons and picked controls show their background look here; with the window in front they take the accent colour.

evaluate: On a small layer, is the depth arrow still easy to catch when you aim at it?
With the playhead on a key, can you see the ring on the layer's middle at a glance?
Does clicking that ring pick the key every time you try it?
On a big layer, does needing to land on the arrow itself feel too fussy?
rough: No mock draws where a press lands: the hit areas follow the nearest-mark rule in docs/design/canvas-hit-order.md, and the ring drawn over the crosshair matches video-move-wt.html, where the rings sit on top of the route.
On the layer itself the arrow now catches only within about 4 points of its line, on every layer, not just small ones. Off the layer it keeps its generous 9 points.
A drag that starts within 6 points of a small layer's edge still resizes it from that edge. That is the edge's own resize band, not the arrow.

A picked ring under the resting pointer still shows the blue hover look instead of white until the pointer moves (right half of 2026-10-16-press-lands-ring-closeup.png), as the 2026-10-13 key dot audit already said.
